selection.name: GitHub Agentic Workflows (C06)
selection.role: Provisional selection for running both agents with a consistent permission boundary. Use v0.89.21, with separate workflows selecting engine: claude and engine: codex, explicit PR/issue triggers, and explicitly scoped safe-outputs. This is a capability and architecture judgment; measured review quality and cost superiority are not established.
selection.install_command:
gh extension install github/gh-aw --pin v0.89.21
gh aw version

basis.shows: Both requested clients are built-in engines. Claude supports ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or workload identity federation; Codex supports CODEX_API_KEY or OPENAI_API_KEY. Engine selection, tool permissions and execution limits are documented.

The documented architecture separates agent execution with read-only GitHub permissions from subsequent jobs with scoped write permissions. The default Linux runtime places the agent in a Docker container with proxy-controlled egress; MCP servers have separate containment. These documented controls are the principal reason for selecting it.

Writes are requested through structured outputs and performed by separate permission-controlled jobs. A material default requires attention: omitting safe-outputs automatically enables limited issue creation. Least-privilege deployment therefore requires explicit output configuration.
An upstream test suite and supported test commands are present, including make test-unit-all. This establishes test infrastructure, not a successful test result on the target host.

Public CI defines tagged Go integration tests, coverage collection and tests of unauthenticated public-workflow retrieval. The sampled check suites did not establish a completed passing result for this pin.

The latest stable release returned by the API was published on 2026-09-23, within 90 days. Its tag resolves to c35393777e5604a63721d09512263b1383301d4f. Published assets include linux-amd64 and darwin-arm64.

Upstream documents the GitHub CLI extension install, compilation into GitHub Actions workflows, and Linux, macOS and Windows-with-WSL authoring support. The documented API-based engines imply that the RTX 4090 is unnecessary for this layer.
The latest default-branch commit was dated 2026-10-02T01:47:17Z, still October 1 in the user's timezone and within the 90-day maintenance window.
The repository is not archived. The API identifies the license as MIT; license was treated as information only.
Recent issue creation and closure activity is visible. This sampled issue is automated activity and does not establish human responsiveness or review accuracy.

not_selected.name: claude-code-action (StepSecurity)
not_selected.reason: Active: default-branch commit 2026-10-01 and release v1.0.183 on 2026-08-12; settings and wrapper tests passed. It covers Claude only and adds a subscription-service check for private repositories, without reviewed comparative evidence establishing a better two-agent solution. [Action source](https://github.com/step-security/claude-code-action/blob/f921413b67d5/action.yml), [passing tests](https://github.com/step-security/claude-code-action/actions/runs/36870692705/job/110397372573).

not_selected.name: codex-action (OpenAI)
not_selected.reason: A close alternative when paired with Anthropic's action: documented privilege reduction and sandbox controls, with a passing verify check. Its latest default-branch commit is 2026-08-20; the latest-stable-release endpoint returned 404. I provisionally prefer gh-aw's shared permission and network architecture for both agents. [README](https://github.com/openai/codex-action/blob/86365089eb2b/README.md), [verify CI](https://github.com/openai/codex-action/actions/runs/32429534752/job/96618203279).

not_selected.name: claude-codex-actions
not_selected.reason: A credible alternative covering both clients, with isolated CLI state and passing contract/scenario CI. Release v1.0.0 reports nine parser/contract tests and twelve synthetic CLI scenarios; these establish wrapper behavior, not live review quality. Permission configuration remains substantially with the caller. Commit and release are from 2026-09-10. [README](https://github.com/andrii-artemenko-gen/claude-codex-actions/blob/f28024429881/README.md), [release](https://github.com/andrii-artemenko-gen/claude-codex-actions/releases/tag/v1.0.0), [passing CI](https://github.com/andrii-artemenko-gen/claude-codex-actions/actions/runs/34486107507).

not_selected.name: No additional component
not_selected.reason: The packet supplies no comparison establishing that neither agent is needed, and this option provides no implementation to assess. Retain it as a control in the deciding trial; the incremental value of agent execution remains unmeasured.

not_selected.name: codex-action (iCoreTech)
not_selected.reason: Active, with a 2026-10-01 default-branch commit and v0.9.48 release. It provides a Linux Docker-based Codex runner, but network_access=false is explicitly documented as a prompt-level policy, making that particular control weaker evidence for least privilege than an enforced network boundary; it also covers only Codex. [README](https://github.com/icoretech/codex-action/blob/ff40c1183874/README.md), [action inputs](https://github.com/icoretech/codex-action/blob/ff40c1183874/action.yml).

not_selected.reason: A close alternative when paired with OpenAI's action, with direct PR/issue integration and documented setup. It covers Claude only; the selected orchestrator documents a common permission boundary across both engines. Maintenance is current through a 2026-10-01 default-branch commit, although the latest-release endpoint returned v1 published on 2025-08-26. [README](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code-action/blob/97c53473391b/README.md), [latest release](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code-action/releases/tag/v1).

not_selected.name: multi-llm-security-review
not_selected.reason: Active, with a 2026-10-01 commit and 1.0.4 release, plus passing check CI. [README](https://github.com/shaztechio/multi-llm-security-review/blob/e22b5fd0d480/README.md), [passing CI](https://github.com/shaztechio/multi-llm-security-review/actions/runs/36894031611/job/110476393292).

not_selected.name: CodeForge
not_selected.reason: Active, with a 2026-09-17 commit and v1.1.3 release, and passing test, integration and end-to-end CI. Its own security model documents agents executing with approvals disabled in the server container, without per-session filesystem or network isolation; that is a weaker fit for this layer's least-privilege requirement. [Security model](https://github.com/freema/codeforge/blob/ef50634085b7/README.md#security-model), [passing CI](https://github.com/freema/codeforge/actions/runs/35197207050).

excluded.name: claude-code-base-action
excluded.fact: The repository explicitly identifies itself as an automated mirror of the base-action directory in anthropics/claude-code-action and directs contributions to that repository. Its current commit, dated 2026-10-01, records that synchronization. It adds no independent complementary component. [Mirror declaration](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code-base-action/blob/4bd489c7d926/README.md).

layers.deciding_comparison: Run four arms on the same fixed PR and issue corpus: gh-aw v0.89.21 using both engines; the OpenAI and Anthropic action pair at the inspected commits; claude-codex-actions v1.0.0 using both clients; and no additional component. Hold agent versions, models, prompts and task budgets constant across agent-enabled arms. Use fresh Linux x86_64 GitHub Actions runners under WSL2 with the required Docker setup. Measure human-confirmed actionable findings, false positives, successful issue-task completion, effective GitHub permissions, filesystem/network access, provider and runner cost per task, and failures. Include controlled untrusted-input fixtures to test permission boundaries. Smoke-test authoring and compilation separately on macOS arm64. This trial would determine whether the integrated controls justify gh-aw's additional machinery and whether either agent adds enough value to justify its cost.
evidence_gaps: No all-arm review-quality, permission or cost comparison was supplied in the packet or found in the fetched upstream READMEs and releases. The selection is provisional; no measured superiority is claimed.

For gh-aw, the first eight sampled check suites on both the release commit and current default-branch commit were QUEUED with no check runs. This sample establishes neither a passing nor a failing CI result. Several other candidates also had queued suites; Anthropic's observed successful mirror-sync job was not treated as a test-suite result.

WSL2 authoring support and Linux/macOS release assets are documented, but installation and agent execution were not tested on the target hosts. macOS arm64 support is established for the gh-aw CLI, not for the Linux Docker security runtime.

The selected engines require CI-specific provider authentication. Reuse of workstation logins or subscription credentials was not verified, and cost per run remains unmeasured. Repository visibility is unspecified, so StepSecurity's private-repository subscription check does not justify a general needs_paid_service exclusion.

All nine repositories were unarchived and had default-branch commits within 90 days. Issue activity was sampled, not evaluated for response latency. Old latest-release records for the Anthropic repositories were not treated as staleness because their default branches are current.

Research used 30 GitHub API calls, including one failed GraphQL request, one web-search query and two blocked page-fetch attempts. Both ctx_fetch_and_index calls returned 'MCP tool call requires approval, but approval policy is never.' Consequently, the required webpage-fetch method could not be completed. Original upstream files were instead retrieved through gh api, indexed with ctx_index and read with ctx_search; no local repository records other than the supplied packet were read.
